title: Electric light control experiment (15 subjects, 4 classes, 31 EEG ch)
description: EEG dataset from 15 healthy participants performing a P300-based brain-computer interface task to control an electric light home appliance. Signals were recorded from 31 scalp channels at 500 Hz while participants viewed flashing visual stimuli on an LCD display in a four-class oddball paradigm with target and non-target events. The recordings support research on ERP-based BCIs for home appliance control and inter-subject transfer learning.
methods_description: EEG was recorded with an actiCHamp (Brain Products) active-electrode system using 31 channels in the standard 10-20 montage, sampled at 500 Hz and referenced to linked mastoids. Each subject completed one session with 50 training and 30 testing blocks. Visual flash stimuli were presented with a 750 ms stimulus onset asynchrony, with online visual feedback.
